subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Aquatics, Alternative, and Adapted Activity Options
title: Performance task build: alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others under transfer
focus: alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others
essentialQuestion: What does an activity look like when it is designed for a different body than mine?
materials: varies by activity; a no-cost, no-facility option is always provided
privacySafeScenario: Trial two activity forms new to the learner — at least one adapted or alternative form — and produce an access analysis identifying what would make each sustainable.
studentTask: Learner works alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others by taking an activity the learner already does and redesigning it for a body or an access situation that is not their own at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others by taking an activity the learner already does and redesigning it for a body or an access situation that is not their own, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Aquatics is optional and always substitutable; no learner is required to enter water. Every activity form has a dry-land, indoor, and zero-cost alternative.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Aquatics is optional and always substitutable; no learner is required to enter water. Every activity form has a dry-land, indoor, and zero-cost alternative.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
